reader_question: Where did the money for 2024 House campaigns come from, and where did it go?
grade_line: Documented: House campaigns’ reports to the Federal Election Commission
title: Individuals gave 2024 House campaigns $1,384.1 million, more than any other source, and the campaigns spent $2,045.3 million.
measure_line: Money into and out of every House candidate’s campaign committees together, 2023 to 2024 election cycle, millions of dollars, not adjusted for inflation; a band’s width is its dollars
notes: No dollar received is traced to a dollar spent: the node holds all 1,926 House candidates’ committees together, primary losers included.

Cash on hand at the start and the end of the cycle let the node balance. The reports leave $1.5 million unaccounted for, 0.059 percent of the money in, where a campaign’s cash figures come from reports that cover different dates.
Loans and their repayments stand apart, so a loan does not read as a gift. Transfers between a candidate’s own committees are netted; on the way out they came to $0, so no band draws.
alt: Bands of money flowing into one node for all 2024 House campaigns and out of it, each as wide as its dollars. In: cash on hand at the start, $355.3 million; individuals, $1,384.1 million; PACs and other committees, $429.9 million; candidates’ loans, $228.5 million; and smaller lines. Out: spending, $2,045.3 million; refunds, loan repayments; and cash on hand at the end, $487.8 million.
